subject: Clarify BAA scope & PHI handling for Redwood (hosted vs dedicated/private)
messages:

Subject: HIPAA BAA and PHI handling questions for Redwood inference usage

Hi Rishi,

We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will include clinical notes and device telemetry that could be considered PHI. A few quick questions to help our security and procurement teams: 

- Do you offer a BAA for customers that need HIPAA coverage?
- Can the hosted (public API) service accept PHI, or do we need Dedicated/Private deployment?
- What logs are retained (request/response content, audit trails), and who has access?
- Is there support for bringing our own KMS and isolating the data plane in our VPC?

We can share expected volume (est. 10k short text requests/day) and sample payload types if that helps. Please CC legal/security as needed.

Thanks,
Dr. Emily Stone

Emily / Rishi — quick technical summary so procurement/security has concrete controls: 

1) Hosted API (public endpoint): not recommended for production PHI. While traffic is encrypted in transit and encrypted at rest, the control plane and multi-tenant runtime are shared; request/response content can be logged for debugging/metrics unless explicitly disabled. We can limit or disable data retention on request, but the safest path for PHI is Dedicated or Private.

2) Dedicated deployment: provides reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation at the runtime level, and can be configured to restrict logs and persist only minimal audit records. Network egress stays in provider region unless configured otherwise. You can request KMS integration (BYOK) for encryption keys.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem): complete control over the data plane, option for on-prem packaging, and full audit logs retained within your environment. This is the only mode where Redwoods control plane is separated and you manage network boundaries entirely.

4) KV cache / caching: we do not persist prompt/response caches beyond configured TTLs for dedicated/private when requested; hosted has more conservative defaults to assist with performance.

5) Logs & access: access to stored logs is limited to specific SRE/Support roles under role-based access control and requires an internal approval workflow. We can provide scoped access tokens for troubleshooting.

6) SOC 2 & audit evidence: we maintain SOC 2 Type II documentation and can provide relevant artifacts under NDA / procurement.

Ive attached our HIPAA security profile and a simplified network topology that shows where data resides in each deployment option. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through specifics and map to your control set.

Attachments: HIPAA_security_profile.pdf, network_topology.png

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Emily — thanks for reaching out. Attached is our standard BAA draft (BAA_Draft_Redwood_v1.docx). A few notes for procurement/legal: 

- Scope: the draft assumes customer will not send direct identifiers to the hosted public API. If you need Redwood to be a \"business associate\" processing PHI, we need to confirm deployment mode (Dedicated or Private) and appropriate security settings.
- Subprocessing: we name our cloud provider in the BAA; if HealthBridge requires a specific cloud contract flow we can append an addendum.
- Audit rights: typical annual SOC 2 evidence sharing is allowed; full penetration-test reports are handled under a controlled sharing process.

Please review the draft and let us know (a) whether you want Redwood to be in-scope as a business associate, and (b) which deployment you prefer so we can finalize the scope. If helpful, we can pre-populate the signature block and route to DocuSign.

Warmly,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: BAA_Draft_Redwood_v1.docx

Monica / Rishi / Dev — thanks for the thorough responses and the draft BAA. A few follow-ups from our side before procurement moves forward: 

- Confirmed scope: HealthBridge expects Redwood to be a business associate for the pilot (we will send direct identifiers). We need written confirmation that Dedicated or Private will be used for PHI processing and that hosted API will be out of scope for PHI.
- BYOK: we will require BYOK (our KMS) for all encryption keys used for PHI storage. Is there a standard integration guide and expected lead time (weeks) to set up a Dedicated deployment in our AWS account?
- Logging: please confirm minimum retention for audit logs and whether debug-level request/response logs can be suppressed permanently for our tenant.
- Evidence: please share the latest SOC 2 Type II report and your most recent penetration test summary. We will treat these as confidential under procurement NDA.

Procurement also provided a checklist and requested a DocuSign-ready BAA so we can route internally. HubSpot deal ID: 1234567.

Timeline: were aiming to have contractual sign-off within two weeks if the technical controls line up. Can we schedule a 30-minute call with Security + Procurement tomorrow afternoon PST?
